A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original recursive-training experiments with GPT-2 and SmolLM2, detector evaluations on MAGE, and experiments on preventing model collapse.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and provides additional performance reporting, including cross-generational training trajectories in Figure S3.

M1.justification: The detector, label smoothing, temperature calibration and weighted sampling procedure remain the same, including weights proportional to (1-q)^b, 1.5-fold sampling and a maximum of 10 selections per sample. Appendix C.1 specifies the previously mentioned threshold-dependent bias; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use English WikiText-2 for open-ended generation and MAGE for text-origin detection, including its four unseen domains and GPT-4 out-of-distribution test. The fully synthetic, partially synthetic and cross-generational scenarios already appear in v1.

E2.justification: v3 Section 5.1 adds an explicit numerical comparison with Longformer, citing Li et al.'s in-distribution and out-of-distribution AUCs of .99 and .94. These are published comparison scores, not newly reported author-run experiments. The three evaluated detector candidates and the training-pool baseline and Oracle remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 reports the GPT-2 base model as 117M parameters, replacing v1's conflicting 128M and 137M descriptions. This revises the reported model-size specification without establishing a different model or rerun. Splits, training budgets, decoding parameters and mixing-coefficient settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure S3 extends the existing cross-generational mixing analysis with trajectories for task performance, text quality and detectability; v1 mainly supplied data-quality endpoints for this setting. v3 Figure S1 largely assembles previously studied mixing scenarios, while v1 Figure S1 is retained as Figure S2.

E5.justification: Both versions specify detector seed 42 in Appendix A.3. Neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests; classifier confidence calibration remains part of the method rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds cross-generational performance results: for GPT-2/top-k at mixing coefficients (0.5,0.5,0.5), final perplexity is 31.33 for the baseline versus 29.47 for the proposed method. Existing fully synthetic scores and all 24 partially synthetic data-quality rows are retained. A new Table S1 entry gives GPT-2/sampling baseline perplexity 38.79 at (1,1,0), conflicting with approximately 30.3 in Figure 2 and yielding Table 3's -25.65%; this is a reporting inconsistency, not an established performance gain between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly defines b = 1 + threshold/(1-threshold), with an odds-ratio rationale and the bound b >= 1. v1 only states that b is calculated from the threshold. The existing recursive-training and weighting equations otherwise retain their mathematical substance; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that decoding strategy affects collapse and detector-guided resampling can prevent it and outperform human-only training when sufficient human data are available. v3's conclusion specifies an equal human/synthetic ratio, a condition already explicitly reported in v1 Section 6.2.

C2.justification: v3 adds a rationale for including deterministic decoding and discusses the diversity-versus-human-likeness tradeoff in GPT-2 sampling. It also introduces misleading explanations: Section 3.5 reverses the neural/metric detector descriptions, and Section 5.3 asserts improvements across all metrics except GPT-2 sampling despite retained SmolLM2 MAUVE declines. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the bias formula, exact MAGE test-set class counts and non-overlapping WikiText chunks. These clarify existing experiments. Conversely, it removes v1's statement that calibration temperature is optimized using negative log-likelihood on the validation set. No new code-access or hardware information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on detector approaches, including RADAR, ConDA, DetectGPT and Binoculars, and mentions Zhu et al.'s token-level editing approach. It also adds the RoBERTa source reference and Longformer performance context. The central positioning around unknown human/synthetic provenance remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial prose editing spans the abstract, introduction, related work and results. v3 merges related-work subsections, moves detector methodology into the Methods section, reorganizes collapse prevention and the appendices, and adds a coauthor and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are extensively revised: Figure 1 becomes a four-panel row, plots receive revised labels and decimal tick values, and Figure 3 is redrawn. Table 1 incorporates v1 Table S1; the mitigation tables gain performance columns and separate generation columns. Additional appendix figures accompany these layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the sampling recipe more reproducible by specifying b, improves the readability of numerical displays, and exposes additional cross-generational performance evidence. These provide a modest overall gain while the central findings remain stable. The gain is tempered by the newly inconsistent 38.79 baseline and derived -25.65% reduction in Tables S1 and 3, overgeneralized result interpretation, and lost calibration-fitting detail; these prevent a stronger improvement assessment.
